FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Paints, 
Varnishes and Related Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 


This standard specifies requirements and method of sampling and test for two component epoxy Micaceous Iron 
Oxide (MIO) pigmented intermediate coat. This material is used for adhesion on inorganic zinc silicate coating 
and epoxy based primers with high toughness and abrasion resistance. This material is used as an intermediate 
coat for painting of steel equipment and steel structures of thermal power plants, where protections from salt 
water, chemicals, mineral oils, solvents and resistance to moisture, protection under marine/refinery conditions 
are required. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding of numerical values (revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


Indian Standard 


TWO COMPONENTS HIGH BUILD EPOXY 
MICACIOUS IRON OXIDE (MIO) PIGMENTED 
INTERMEDIATE COAT — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard specifies the requirements and 
method of sampling and test for two component epoxy 
Micaceous Iron Oxide (MIO) pigmented intermediate 
coat. 


1.2 This material is expected to have adhesion on 
inorganic zinc silicate coating and epoxy based primers 
with high toughness and abrasion resistance. This 
material is used as an intermediate coat for painting 
of steel equipment and steel structures of thermal 
power plants, where protections from salt water, 
chemicals, mineral oils, solvents and resistance to 
moisture, protection under marine/refinery conditions 
are required.

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard the terms and definitions 
used in IS 1303 shall apply. 


4 REQUIREMENT 


4.1 Composition 


Paints complying with this standard shall comprise 
epoxy resin as the principal binder. The manufacturer 
shall specify the principal type of binder used in the 
paint, which shall have epoxy equivalent in the range 
of 350 to 600. A test certificate from a laboratory 
having accreditation against IS/ISO/IEC 17025, shall 
be furnished by the manufacturer reporting micaceous 
iron oxide content by X-ray diffraction method. The 
composition of paint shall be such that it satisfies the 
requirements specified in this standard. 


4.1.1 The paint shall consist essentially of two 
components, base and hardener, or catalyst solution to be 
mixed in the appropriate ratio by volume, as prescribed 
by the manufacturer, to meet the requirements of this 
standard. 


4.2 The material shall also conform to the requirements 
specified in Table 1. 


4.3 Keeping Properties 


The material shall conform to the requirements specified 
in Table 1 when tested after storing for a period of 
minimum one year from the date of manufacture, 
when stored in original sealed containers under normal 
atmospheric conditions. 


5 TESTS 


5.1 Unless specified otherwise, methods of test 
prescribed in IS 101 series of standards shall be 
followed. 


5.2 For all tests, mild steel panels shall be prepared 
except for bend test for which burnished tin plate panels 
shall be used. The preparation of metal panels shall be 
as prescribed in IS 101 (Part 1/Sec 3). 


5.3 Quality of Reagents 


Unless or otherwise specified, analytical reagent grade 
chemicals and reagent grade water (see IS 1070) shall 
be used. 


NOTE — Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 


5.4 Test certificate shall be in a format as agreed 
between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 


6 PACKING AND MARKING 


6.1 Packing 


The material shall be packed in dual containers as 
agreed between the purchaser and the manufacturer. It 
shall be ensured that the quality of material does not 
deteriorate during transit and storage. 


6.2 Marking 


6.2.1 Each container shall be marked with the following 
information: 


a) Indication of the source of manufacture; 
b) Batch/Lot number in code or otherwise; 
c) Month and year of manufacture; 

d) Date of expiry; 

e) Mass of the material; and 

f) Mixing ratio. 


6.2.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark on the container. 


6.2.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act,2016 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details ofthe conditions under which the licence for use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 


7 SAMPLING 


Representative samples shall be drawn as prescribed 
in 6 of IS 101 (Partl/Sec 1).

ANNEX A 
[ Table 1, SI No. (ii) ] 


CONSISTENCY 


A-1 APPARATUS 
A-1.1 Palette Knife or Metal Rod 


A-1.2 Panels 


Unless specified otherwise, steel panels prescribed in 
2 of IS 101 (Part 1/Sec 3) shall be prepared and used. 


A-2 PROCEDURE 


A-2.1 Insert a clean metal rod or palette knife into the 
original container and examine the nature of settling. 


A-2.2 Observations 


The material shall not cake hard inside the container 
and shall be in such a condition that stirring easily 
produces a smooth uniform paint suitable for coating 
on steel 


ANNEX B 
[ Table 1, SI No. (vii) ] 


DETERMINATION OF POT LIFE 


B-1 GENERAL 


The time taken to double the viscosity from the original 
value shall be considered as the pot life of the material. 


B-2 PROCEDURE 


B-2.1 Thoroughly mix component parts in the ratio 
prescribed by the manufacturer to give a sample of 
200 ml by volume. 


B-2.2 Within 10 min of mixing (B-2.1), determine the 
viscosity as prescribed in IS 101 (Part 1/Sec 5). 


B-2.3 Allow the mixed sample of paint to stand in a 
suitable air-tight container and determine the viscosity 
at the end of the specified time.

development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
